Direct detection of null encryption and IMSI disclosure is not implemented for standard Android installations. It requires privileged APIs or permissions that a non-root app does not receive, so this rule is shown as N/A when the system does not expose the data.

Site keys are not anonymous: they are deterministic, unsalted hashes of a ~500 m grid, so anyone can compute the keys of an area and link them to an approximate location. Cell identities, times and counts can also reveal your habits. No exact coordinates or credentials are included. Review the ZIP before sharing it.
The package may contain precise GPS location, radio data, device model and technical logs. Review it before sharing; it never contains API keys, IMSI or IMEI.

On LTE, the Cell ID groups sectors by eNodeB (CID/256). A large separation deserves review, although a logical eNodeB may use remote radio heads and is not always one physical tower.
Cells handing the phone to each other overlap in coverage. The unexplained gap between centres minus both P90 radii should be zero or small. Ordered worst to best.
Sectors grouped under this eNodeB appear far apart. This may indicate reused or anomalous identity, but also a distributed network; review it with the remaining evidence.

Android only shares the serving and neighbour cells (Cell ID, PCI, frequency, signal) with apps that have location access. GPS coordinates also let the app compare each antenna with where it was seen before (H11, H13, H16), record where an incident happened and build the Geometry view. While monitoring runs, location is used continuously by a foreground service with a visible notification.

Needed to follow the network state: operator, registration, service and data-network changes, and the cellular security events Android reports. ICdetection does not read calls, SMS, contacts, your phone number or IMEI.
Shows the ongoing monitoring notification and warns you when an anomaly is confirmed. You can deny it: monitoring still works, but you will not see alerts outside the app.

The Security alerts channel is silent, so the notification of a confirmed network anomaly will arrive without sound. Turn its sound back on: ICdetection only makes a sound when a network anomaly is confirmed, and the monitoring notification is always silent. The short alert tone is separate and still plays unless the phone is on silent, vibrate or Do Not Disturb.

ICdetection notifications are turned off, so a confirmed network anomaly will not appear as a notification. Turn them back on: ICdetection only makes a sound when a network anomaly is confirmed, and the monitoring notification is always silent. The short alert tone is separate and still plays unless the phone is on silent, vibrate or Do Not Disturb.
Keeps GPS requests active with the screen on or off. Recommended for field campaigns where location continuity matters. Uses more battery, including where GPS reception is poor.

Continuous GPS while the screen is on and reception is available. With the screen off, requests are limited to cell changes, suspected anomalies and returning to the phone. After repeated failures it pauses and checks again every 2, 5 or 10 minutes. Location-dependent rules may be N/A more often.

Requests a fresh GPS fix about every 45 seconds, including with the screen off. A change to a new cell always wakes the GPS and keeps it active until 60 seconds after the last new cell, so it stays on during a journey; hopping between known cells at rest does not keep it on. Outside these windows, each attempt stops after a fix or 20 seconds (45 seconds for the first). After repeated failures it checks again every 2, 5 or 10 minutes; a new cell still gets a short attempt, at most one per minute. A fresh fix restores the normal schedule. Cellular scanning continues, but a GPS position for every cell cannot be guaranteed. Battery savings depend on reception.

Saves all ICdetection data (history, antennas, incidents, forensic cases, Stable-Site and trips) and your settings in one file. The file is not encrypted and contains your location history: keep it private.
Restoring REPLACES all current data. Before replacing anything, you save a copy of your current data wherever you choose.

Learns how the signal of each cell usually looks on THIS phone and records, for every saved row, how far the observation is from it. It always runs in the background (shadow) and goes into the CSV export. Turning this on only shows the latest evaluation here: it does not add, silence or lower alerts, and it is not proof of an IMSI catcher.

Your phone is using a 2G/3G network. This can happen with weak 4G/5G coverage or during calls without VoLTE; it is not a confirmed attack. Use Airplane mode settings if you want to leave the network.

One alert when the phone starts using 2G/3G; no repeats while it stays there. A new alert needs at least 1 minute in a row back on 4G/5G first. It can be caused by coverage or calls without VoLTE. If your phone offers an «Allow 2G» setting, turning it off avoids 2G (not 3G). Airplane mode is always your own choice.
